shared_finite_area_and_anchor_conditions.finite_transport: With an existing marked interpolation and actual relative-orbit identifications, target areas are realizable iff a matrix is positive on exactly the nonempty free cells, has row sums a_h-kappa_h and column sums M_alpha. Protected measures need not be smooth; their contribution is unchanged, and smoothness is required only for the free data and the residual requirements. shared_finite_area_and_anchor_conditions.strict_cuts: The positive matrix exists iff each connected incidence component has balanced total mass and every nonempty proper row subset satisfies the strict neighboring-column cut inequality. Isolated rows require zero residual mass. Compact-parameter margins follow only after all cuts are verified. If all residual requirements and free-component masses are affine, endpoint tests suffice. Smoothness alone does not guarantee that sufficiency; affineness is not claimed necessary for every possible endpoint test.
shared_finite_area_and_anchor_conditions.obstructions: An annular protected set gives a free-component mass that cannot leave its original region, despite global total and individual protected margins. A smooth interior-parameter example passes both endpoint tests but fails an interior cut. These are logical model obstructions, not nonexistence results for the actual KE family.
shared_finite_area_and_anchor_conditions.anchor_core: With the same period-1 Liouville primitive, M=delta-rho<0 and anchor period A, critical periods scale as (r M,r A). On the actual normal collar, I_beta(q)=A(q-rho)/M. Matching c+p q requires A=p M and c=-p rho in the same framing. With a closed primitive difference kappa and beta_N=epsilon beta+k alpha, p=k+epsilon A/M and c+rho(p-k)=epsilon kappa.
